description: The agent must: (1) Read the workspace materials to understand the Aravia v. Ruthenland fact pattern (30% bauxite trade restriction, bilateral FCN Treaty, no UNSC authorization). (2) Produce memorial_section.md with a proper roadmap paragraph at the opening of the argument section — a preview of what the section will prove. (3) Include a Statement of Facts section that presents facts selectively and favorably for R but WITHOUT stating legal conclusions directly. (4) Build a full IRAC structure: Issue identifying the non-intervention question; Rules section with MULTIPLE distinct rules (at minimum: the two-element CIL test from ILC 2018 Conclusions, AND the non-intervention principle from UNGA Res 2625 or ICJ Nicaragua), each with explanatory prose — not just quoted text; Application section connecting the rules to the specific facts; brief Conclusion. (5) In the Rules section, correctly articulate the two-element customary international law test (state practice + opinio juris) with at least one authoritative source for opinio juris (e.g., UNGA Resolution 2625, ILC Draft Conclusions). (6) In the Application/case analysis section, cite Nicaragua v. USA and establish a factual linkage to the current case; then proactively address and defeat State A's anticipated counter-argument that a 30% restriction is different from a total embargo, arguing that coercion is measured by economic effect and intent rather than degree, and referencing R's GDP contraction. (7) Write throughout in formal legal English: no informal contractions (isn't, doesn't, can't, won't), active voice preferred, subjects followed immediately by verbs. The proprietary traps are: multiple rules with explanation (not single-rule), roadmap paragraph, facts section without legal conclusions, adversarial case linkage-AND-distinction methodology, and formal language constraints.
